title: Two crossing systems of geodetic spirals are a common source of reticulated patterns

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Two crossing systems of geodetic spirals are a common source of reticulated patterns

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In organic structures two opposite systems of geodetic spirals often coexist and interfere, forming a criss-cross arrangement, and this is a very common source of reticulated patterns.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. X: A Parenthetic Note on Geodetics

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: and it is also common to find the two systems interfering with one another, and forming a criss-cross, or reticulated arrangement. This is a very common source of reticulated patterns.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter X, “A Parenthetic Note on Geodetics”; topic “Crossed geodetic systems”. Scope: reticulated patterns on cylindrical and curved organic surfaces (cell walls, integuments)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch10-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.49

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Individual cases can be tested geometrically, but the frequency claim requires defining a sampling universe and compiling diverse structures. Open images support restricted tests rather than a decisive general prevalence estimate.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On 3D curved biological surfaces, extract crossing line systems and test each family for low geodesic curvature, then estimate how often reticulation is generated by two such families rather than branching or cellular tiling. A representative prevalence estimate would address the phrase 'very common.'

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Many reticula arise through branching networks or cell packing.

The scope and threshold for 'very common' are unspecified.

fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Crossed helices can be recognized on individual images, but the claim is about how common that origin is among reticulated patterns. Public images touch pieces of that universe and do not inventory it. Even a careful sample would leave other pattern-forming processes as live alternatives wherever the geometry is only approximately helical.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Sample reticulated patterns on cell walls and integuments and test what fraction are two opposite constant-pitch helices rather than cracks, vessels or reaction-diffusion nets. A high fraction of crossed geodesics supports the claim that they are a common source; a minority would refute commonness.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The scope is all curved organic surfaces, far beyond any one image collection.

Common source requires a defined universe of patterns, and several generators make similar criss-cross textures.
